note: Rewritten from Sands' (1999) new species description, original in English; the genus lacks soldiers, only the worker has a complete description; measurements follow the original ranges; the author placed the comparisons of this species with the preceding ones under the names of those species.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: From A. multispinus it differs in that the legs are distinctly longer, the first marginal tooth of the left mandible is nearly equilateral, the fourth marginal tooth does not touch the molar prominence, the enteric valve ridges are taper-ellipsoid rather than waisted, the ridges differ in degree of sclerotization (ridge one colourless, ridge three pale brown apically), with fewer, straight conical spines on ridges one and three, and the valve is bilaterally symmetrical. The author placed the comparisons of this species with the preceding ones under the names of those species.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow, the darkest part of the antennal flagellum pale yellow or yellow, pronotum and legs yellowish white, abdominal tergites transparent. Head capsule oval, setae sparse, projecting, the longest setae arranged regularly and symmetrically. Fontanelle absent. Anterior surface of the fore coxa with 3 or more stout setae arranged in rows or groups; fore tibia with 3 distal spurs, the third well developed, at least one-half the length of the others. Left mandible: first marginal tooth nearly equilateral, anterior margin of the third marginal tooth as long as that of the first marginal tooth, the proximal end of the fourth marginal tooth not touching the molar prominence in frontal view; right mandible: anterior margin of the first marginal tooth shorter than that of the second marginal tooth. Measurements: head width 0.696—0.706 mm; pronotum width 0.438—0.460 mm, length 0.233—0.239 mm; hind tibia length 0.784—0.794 mm; fore tibia length 0.620—0.625 mm; left mandible index 0.855—0.88, right mandible index 1.069—1.149.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The midgut–hindgut junction arises ventrally below the nerve cord; the first hindgut segment is rather short, up to 8 times as long as its proximal width, tubular throughout; in the undissected abdomen the enteric valve lies to the right of the heart (dorsal view) or to the left of the nerve cord (ventral view); the third lobe of the enteric valve seat is smaller than the outer pair. The enteric valve ridges are nearly taper-ellipsoid from the base towards the apical spines, not waisted: ridge one unsclerotized or colourless throughout, ridges two and four weakly sclerotized and pale yellow or yellow apically, ridge three sclerotized and pale brown or yellowish brown apically; the primary rows of all ridges consist of large, upright, backward-directed conical spines, at most 14 on ridges one and two, 15—20 on ridge three and 1—9 on ridge four, the longest straight and evenly tapering.
